items.stem: Which opening best suits an OET-style referral letter to a specialist?

options.text: A concise statement of the reason for referral and the main clinical concern
options.rationale: Correct: states purpose and principal problem for the reader to act on.

options.text: A detailed restatement of the patient's entire record
options.rationale: Full record restatement buries the purpose and is not concise.

options.text: A list of the writing doctor's publications
options.rationale: Irrelevant to a clinical referral's purpose.

items.explanation: Correct: states purpose and principal problem for the reader to act on.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: During a consultation role-play, a patient appears anxious. Which approach best fits patient-centred communication?

options.text: Acknowledge the concern, explain clearly and check understanding
options.rationale: Correct: empathy, clarity and confirmation are central to the criteria.

options.text: Speed up to finish the consultation quickly
options.rationale: Rushing ignores the patient's concern and reduces clarity.
Jargon without explanation is not patient-centred.
Withholding relevant information does not meet the communicative purpose.

items.explanation: Correct: empathy, clarity and confirmation are central to the criteria.

items.stem: Which TWO are assessed strengths of an effective OET-style medical referral letter?

options.text: Clear statement of the purpose of writing
options.rationale: Correct: purpose clarity is a core criterion.
Correct: relevance and selection are assessed.
Length is not a criterion; concise relevance is.
Overuse of unexplained abbreviations harms clarity.

options.text: Omitting the diagnosis to save space
options.rationale: Key clinical facts must be included.
